paper.title: Why MSARIMA prediction intervals under-cover on M1, M3 and Tourism

definitions.definition: predict(interval='prediction') for a pure ARIMA of smooth: dispatches to 'approximate', variance s2*T/df * diag(covar_anal) with normal quantiles, around the point forecast (python/src/smooth/adam_general/core/forecaster/intervals.py generate_prediction_interval).

Gaussian ARIMA series with sigma=10 generated in numpy from polynomials independent of smooth: 11 DGPs (rw, ima, ar1, ma1, arima111, ima22, rwd, imad, airline12, airline4, sar12), T in 50,100,300, h 1-18.
T: true orders and true AR/MA/constant, initial states and scale estimated. E: true orders, estimated parameters. S: AutoMSARIMA selected orders. Each with initial=backcasting and initial=optimal.
Share of holdout actuals inside the two-sided interval (cov80, cov95) or below the quantile (q10, q50, q90), averaged over horizons, then over replicates.
5,315 series of M1, M3 and Tourism from fcompdata 0.1.4, with the harness of 2026-11-05-smooth-1-3-0-benchmark_auto_arima.ipynb.

1500 series each of M4 yearly, quarterly and monthly (fcompdata load_m4, Zenodo tsf files), drawn with numpy default_rng(20261105); none is in the benchmark sets as loaded, though M4 may share sources with M3.
Series split into terciles of mean(last third of the in-sample data)/mean(in-sample data); cov80 averaged over the series of each tercile.

R auto.adam(y, model="NNN", lags, distribution=c("dnorm","dlnorm"), initial="backcasting"): ARIMA orders and constant selected for each distribution with the default maxima of auto.msarima, then the distribution with the lower AICc; intervals from forecast(interval="prediction"). Compared with auto.msarima, which fixes dnorm.
1500 series each of M4 yearly, quarterly and monthly, drawn with seed 20261107 from the series not drawn by seed 20261105 (the M4 sample of PL12 and PL13), so disjoint from it.

claims.statement: With true orders and true parameters, the [[D1:MSARIMA analytic interval]] of smooth reaches its nominal [[D4:coverage]] in the [[D2:known-model simulation]] at T of 100 and 300, and its width equals the theoretical h-step width.

parameters.sample: 2000 replicates per cell, h=1..18, fixed seed 20261105, no interim analysis

claims.statement: With selected orders, the [[D1:MSARIMA analytic interval]] loses little [[D4:coverage]] in the [[D2:known-model simulation]] at T=100 against the 12 points missing on the benchmark: pooled cov80 of case S with backcasting is 0.77 or above.

Stated by the human; the agent had seen RN2.

claims.statement: Scenario c: a wrong model alone produces under-coverage of the size seen on the benchmark: pooled 80% [[D4:coverage]] of the [[D1:MSARIMA analytic interval]] over the 12 wrong models of the [[D2:known-model simulation]] at T=100 is 0.72 or below.

claims.statement: On the 5,315 benchmark series, reforecast() closes at least half of the gap of the 80% [[D4:coverage]] of the [[D1:MSARIMA analytic interval]] from 0.80, with a pinball no more than 1% worse.

parameters.sample: All 5,315 series, seed per series, nsim=300; run only after the verdict of the plan testing reforecast() in simulation

claims.statement: The [[D1:MSARIMA analytic interval]] under-covers because the error scale grows with the level: its constant variance is too small at the origin of series whose level has risen. Its 80% [[D4:coverage]] falls from the lowest to the highest tercile of recent level over mean level by at least 10 points, while ETS(MNN) falls by at most 5.

evidence.description: Lab runs RN6 under plan PL4. Design: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q1_simulate.py --n 2000 --seed 20261105 --workers 30 --cases T_backcasting T_optimal; 11 DGPs, T=50,100,300. Analysis: Coverage of the 99 quantiles, width over the theoretical h-step width; MCE on the coverage pooled over DGPs and largest cell MCE. Decision at T=100 and 300; T=50 reported.

Lab runs RN11 under plan PL5. Design: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q1_simulate.py --n 2000 --seed 20261105 --workers 30 --cases S_backcasting S_optimal. Analysis: Scenario b. Pooled cov80, MCE and relative pinball by T; decision on S_backcasting at T=100, 74-77% inconclusive.

Lab runs RN7 under plan PL6. Design: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q1_simulate.py --n 2000 --seed 20261105 --workers 30 --cases E_backcasting E_backcasting_sim. Analysis: predict(interval='prediction') and predict(interval='simulated') on the same fit: pooled width and MCE at T=50,100,300.

Lab runs RN8 under plan PL7. Design: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q1_simulate.py --n 2000 --seed 20261105 --workers 30 --cases T_backcasting E_backcasting T_optimal E_optimal; same series for all cases. Analysis: Scenario a. cov80 of T minus cov80 of E at T=100 decides; T=50,300 and MCE reported.

Lab runs RN9 under plan PL8. Design: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q1_simulate.py --n 2000 --seed 20261105 --workers 30 --cases E_backcasting E_backcasting_ref E_optimal E_optimal_ref; reforecast nsim=300; on a model with no parameter (rw with backcasting) reforecast raises and the interval is predict's. Analysis: Pooled MCE and pinball relative to the oracle at T=100 decide, for both initials.

Lab runs RN10 under plan PL9. Design: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q1_simulate.py --n 2000 --seed 20261105 --workers 30 --dgps rw ima ar1 ma1 arima111 ima22 rwd imad airline12 airline4 sar12 ima_t4 --cases W_backcasting W_backcasting_ref; wrong models listed in WRONG of the script. Analysis: Scenario c. Pooled cov80 at T=100 decides, with cov80, q50, MCE and width per mistake reported; the pool of mistakes is a choice, not a sample of real mistakes.

Lab runs RN12 under plan PL10. Design: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q1_benchmark_reforecast.py --workers 30 --saved python/tests/notebooks/2026-11-05-benchmark-arima-smooth-1-3-0-coverage.npy, from the main checkout's saved array; AutoMSARIMA back and opt; predict and reforecast (nsim=300) on the same fit. Analysis: Backcasting decides, cov80 and pinball; optimal, MCE and q50 reported. The predict coverage must match the saved array, reported as their mean absolute difference.

results.variable: mean absolute difference of the predict coverage from the saved array

evidence.description: Lab runs RN41 under plan PL12. Design: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q4_m4.py --methods auto force_mnn: AutoMSARIMA with backcasting against ETS(MNN) forced, backcasting, 99 quantiles. Analysis: cov80 per series, mean per level tercile; fall = low minus high tercile.

Lab runs RN42 under plan PL13. Design: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q4_m4.py --methods auto auto_dlnorm: AutoMSARIMA, then ADAM(model=NNN) with its orders and constant and distribution=dlnorm, backcasting. Analysis: MCE over the 99 levels and the spread (max minus min) of cov80 over the level terciles; pinball median and mean reported, not decisive.

Lab runs RN43, RN44 under plan PL11. Design: Run 1: smooth-v108 worktree at v1.0.8-py, its python/.venv. Run 2: python/.venv (1.3.0). Both: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q1_simulate.py --n 2000 --seed 20261105 --workers 30 --cases T_backcasting E_backcasting S_backcasting E_optimal. Analysis: Pooled MCE at T=100 per case; T=50, 300, cov80 and width reported.

Lab runs RN47 under plan PL14. Design: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q5_autoadam.py --data m4 --seed 20261107 --exclude-seed 20261105: R auto.msarima and R auto.adam(model=NNN, distribution=c(dnorm, dlnorm)), backcasting, on the fresh M4 sample of 4500 series, 99 quantiles per series. Analysis: MCE over the 99 levels of each method; spread (max minus min) of cov80 over the level terciles; pinball median and mean, share choosing dlnorm reported, not decisive.

Lab runs RN48 under plan PL15. Design: As PL14, rerun because PL14's run failed on missing data: python claimset-code/msarima-interval-calibration/q5_autoadam.py --data m4 --seed 20261107 --exclude-seed 20261105: R auto.msarima and R auto.adam(model=NNN, distribution=c(dnorm, dlnorm)), backcasting, on the fresh M4 sample of 4500 series, 99 quantiles per series. M4 files passed with --data so their hashes are recorded. Analysis: MCE over the 99 levels of each method; spread (max minus min) of cov80 over the level terciles; pinball median and mean, share choosing dlnorm reported, not decisive.
